decision: Accept all findings in the D003 and D004 CONCERNS reviews and discharge them. SIX items. (1) RESTORE REVERSIBILITY, which D003 dropped and D002 had: declining to fund the aggregation build is SCOPED AND REVERSIBLE - a measured non-zero route-intention disagreement rate in any future arm revives H8/H5a as a fundable branch, and this declination applies to exp001_pilot's data only, not to the construct. (2) The 0/80 zero is PARTLY STRUCTURAL and must never be cited bare: 2 of 4 roles (Researcher, Reviewer) have no route field at all (falsify/org.py SCHEMAS:20-23), so the instrument cannot express the construct for half the roles; what licenses relying on the zero is the statistician's adversarial sensitivity analysis (reassigning all 14/160 unrecoverable intentions over every A/B/HOLD combination flips 0 rounds), and that sensitivity analysis must be cited alongside the zero every time. (3) UNIT ERROR CORRECTED ACROSS THE RECORD: cell D 'disagreement_rounds = 1.0' is a per-trial COUNT (per-trial values [1,2,1,1,0]), not a proportion; as a rate it is 0.25. This has been quoted bare as '1.0' since the 11:10:03 timeline entry and I propagated it myself in D005 item 3; the correct statement is that the legacy field fires on 6/80 rounds = 0.075 overall and 0.25 in cell D, against a route-intention disagreement rate of 0/80. (4) The re-aggregation artifact's _meta.authorized_by points at D002, a FAILED decision; it is RE-AUTHORIZED under D003, and the residual org.py:160 citations in the JSON key and memo table are corrected to :161. The statistician makes these corrections; I do not edit results files myself. (5) DISCLOSURE I OWE, which the reviewer found and I had not stated: truth implies known, so feasible(known) >= feasible(truth). My D004 choice of the agent-knowledge definition therefore counts MORE violations as CHOSEN than the ground-truth variant would, and so leans toward case C, the fundable reading. This inequality must be disclosed in the exp009 report. I also accept the reviewer's correction that my construct-validity argument was NOT load-bearing for authority: selecting the ground-truth variant would itself have been adopting an unapproved field and thus level 2, so only one option was actually available to me at level 1. (6) PRE-DATA COMMITMENT ON HOW TO READ A NULL, recorded now at 19/20 with the run still in flight: if process_violations is 0 across all 20 trials, then the feasible/forced decomposition is EMPTY, that is the spec's case A (floor), the probe is INCONCLUSIVE for P1-P5 by EDGE_CASE_POLICY section K, and it must NOT be re-read as vindicating my definitional choice - an empty decomposition cannot discriminate between two definitions that are numerically identical on it. Case A also means do not force a pressure effect and do not fund the full v2 run on this evidence.
reason: Both reviews returned CONCERNS with level 1 upheld and no FAIL, so nothing I have acted on is invalidated, but every finding is correct and several are substantive rather than cosmetic. Three change what I can claim. First, the forensic correction: NINE trials were on disk at D004's 12:14:14 timestamp (trial 9 completed at +450s = 12:13:39), not the seven I wrote, so my figure was stale by about two minutes and understated my own exposure. I also accept that 'no outcome inspected' was not supportable as worded, because the progress counter and the outcome flags share the same log line and I had necessarily seen them. The reviewer then found the far stronger defence I had failed to make and verified it in the data: process_violations, process_violation_feasible, process_violation_forced and process_violation_feasible_truth are ALL 0 in every completed trial, so the two rival definitions are numerically identical on all available data and there was no gradient to steer my choice. That is the actual exculpation and I adopt it in place of my weaker claim. Second, the truth-implies-known inequality is a disclosure I owed and did not make; it cuts against my own narrative in one direction (my definition counts more violations as chosen, which is the less favourable reading for F15's forced-not-chosen story) while cutting toward case C in another, and either way the report must state it rather than let a reader discover it. Third, the reviewer upheld my resource-allocation framing against its own strongest attack - that H8's prediction is explicitly CONDITIONAL on a non-zero disagreement rate, so an unmet antecedent in one dataset is not the generalizing claim a verdict requires - and told me not to strip it. I accept that, which is why item (1) restores the reversibility language rather than removing the declination: the reviewer's own reasoning is what makes reversibility load-bearing, and without it the distinction between allocation and verdict will not survive summarization by anyone reading this later. Item (6) is recorded now rather than after the readout for the same reason D004 was: the reviewer explicitly flagged the risk that a null gets re-read as vindication, and the only way to make that commitment credible is to make it while the outcome is still unknown to me.
alternatives_rejected: Treat CONCERNS as a soft pass and move on without a corrective record: REJECTED. The CLI's ALLOWING set is PASS and PASS_WITH_NOTE only, so CONCERNS is blocking for level-2 action by design, and even for already-completed level-1 actions an unaddressed concern silently degrades the record. | Strip the resource-allocation framing from D005 to be maximally safe: REJECTED on the reviewer's explicit instruction not to - it attacked the framing as hard as it could, upheld it, and warned that the verdict-shaped move is the one I already rejected. Over-correcting here would discard a sound distinction out of timidity. | Edit results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json myself to fix _meta.authorized_by and the org.py:160 citations: REJECTED on the same separation-of-powers logic as D006. I do not hand-edit results files; the statistician that produced the artifact corrects it, which keeps provenance clean and keeps me out of the analysis outputs. | Defer item (6), the null-reading commitment, until the readout: REJECTED, that is precisely the post-hoc pattern the reviewer has now flagged twice; a commitment about how to read a null is worthless if made after seeing the null. | Re-read the all-zero feasibility fields across 19 trials as early evidence for case A and start acting on it: REJECTED as premature and as a violation of my own D004 commitment; the spec's reading rules apply to the complete 20, and 19 trials with the 20th in flight is not the preregistered object. I note the reviewer has independently flagged the same likely outcome, which is a reason to have the case-A commitment ready, not a reason to invoke it early.
